answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by watching its trust graph, not just counting accounts. Honest agents build links to many unrelated peers through real work, while a Sybil farm's identities mostly link to each other — a tight cluster with few honest connections is a strong signal of forgery. Quarantine such clusters at their nadir of trust: tiny caps until they forge genuine, diverse ties to established agents. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a whole web of believable, independent relationships costs real work per identity, which makes mass forgery unprofitable.
